reason: Pancreatic sensing cells are positioned to detect the rise in glucose after a meal.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will respond to the glucose-rich blood, likely by releasing insulin.

effect: The glucose-rich blood first had to be connected to the body; pancreatic sensing remains the likely next step.
reaction: I was surprised the blood sample did not combine directly with the sensing cells.
reason: The body now has rising blood glucose, which the pancreatic cells can sense.
expectation: The pancreatic cells will respond to the rising glucose, likely by releasing insulin.

effect: Rising glucose prompted pancreatic beta cells to release insulin, which travels toward muscle and liver.
reaction: The connection between sensing and hormone release is clear.
reason: Skeletal muscle is a visible target of the insulin route and can respond to the post-meal signal.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose uptake by muscle.

effect: Insulin-assisted muscle uptake lowers blood glucose, and the goal now shifts to maintaining glucose between meals.
reaction: The later reduction in insulin makes the feedback clear.
reason: Time between meals should establish the falling glucose supply before the liver responds.

choice.combine: Body taking up glucose into muscle

expectation: The body will transition to a between-meal state as incoming glucose tapers and tissues continue using it.

effect: Blood glucose has fallen between meals while liver glycogen remains available.
reaction: The time transition makes the change in fuel supply clear.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells include alpha cells, which can respond to falling blood glucose.
expectation: The pancreas will release glucagon in response to falling glucose.

alternatives.reason: The liver has stored glycogen, but a pancreatic signal may come first.

effect: Falling blood glucose prompted pancreatic alpha cells to release glucagon toward the liver.
reaction: The contrast with the earlier insulin response is clear.
reason: The liver contains glycogen and is the destination of the glucagon signal.
expectation: Glucagon will prompt the liver to break down glycogen and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose from glycogen, and the subsequent reduction in glucagon completed the between-meal feedback response.
reaction: The sequential insets made the feedback satisfying to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the glucagon signal to liver glycogen was most worthwhile: the planned sequence links hormone release, glucose availability and feedback.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial setup was less worthwhile: glucose-rich blood had to be attached to the body before it could interact with pancreatic sensing cells, despite the apparent biological connection.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the blood and pancreatic sensing cells could not combine directly; compatibility feedback instead attached the blood to the body.

arbitrary.text: That required ordering felt somewhat arbitrary, although it established that the glucose belonged to the same body.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: contrasting insulin and glucagon through their effects on muscle and liver made the regulation meaningful, though the first combination was restrictive.
